OTA Performance Dashboard

POC: Bimpe Abimbola  |  Last Updated: September 2026

Airbnb (ABNB) Booking Holdings (BKNG) Expedia Group (EXPE) Trip.com Group (TCOM)

Performance Trends

Nights Booked — Y/Y Growth

Year-over-year growth in nights/room nights booked (%); gaps = not available

Nights growth has been remarkably stable across peers, hovering 6–13% throughout the 9-quarter window with no clear deceleration trend. Notably, Airbnb's volume growth reaccelerated to +9% in Q1'26 while Booking and Expedia both moderated to +6%, suggesting Airbnb is gaining share in a late-cycle environment.

Gross Bookings / GBV — Y/Y Growth

Year-over-year growth in gross bookings value (%); 2024 quarters derived from annual growth rates

GBV growth is diverging from nights growth — indicating pricing/mix rather than volume is driving the spread. Airbnb's GBV accelerated to +19% in Q1'26 vs. just +9% nights growth, pointing to the ADR re-inflation driven by the Reserve Now Pay Later program and mix shift toward larger homes.

Revenue — Y/Y Growth

Year-over-year revenue growth rate (%)

After converging near 6–10% in mid-2024 as post-COVID tailwinds normalized, revenue growth reaccelerated for all three reporting peers in Q1'26 to 15–18%. Trip.com is an outlier at +29% in Q1'24, anchored by China's post-lockdown reopening, and its growth has since normalized to ~16–21%.

Revenue

Total net revenue, USD billions

Booking Holdings commands roughly 2× Airbnb and Expedia's revenue at scale, reaching $9B in Q3'24 alone. The gap between Booking and its peers has widened since 2022, reflecting its superior EMEA-weighted portfolio in a period of strong European travel demand.

Gross Bookings / GBV

Total value of bookings; Trip.com not disclosed

Booking's GBV of $53.8B in Q1'26 is nearly 2× Expedia's and 1.8× Airbnb's, underscoring its structural dominance in gross booking flow. Airbnb's GBV growth of +19% Y/Y in Q1'26 was the fastest among peers, narrowing the gap versus Expedia for the first time in recent quarters.

Adjusted EBITDA

USD billions; gaps = data not available

All OTAs show pronounced EBITDA seasonality, with Q3 (summer peak) generating 2–3× Q1 profitability. Expedia's Q1'26 EBITDA of $542M was up +83% Y/Y — a 15-year Q1 record — driven by its cost restructuring program that reduced headcount by ~1,200 in 2024.

Adj EBITDA Margin

Adjusted EBITDA as % of revenue; gaps = data not available

Airbnb's Q3 EBITDA margin has held near 54% for two consecutive years, the highest in the peer group, reflecting its asset-light model and disciplined cost base. Expedia's Q1'26 margin of 15.8% represents a structural improvement from its historical Q1 lows below 10%.

Net Income

GAAP net income, USD billions; limited quarterly disclosure

Booking's Q1'26 net income of $1.10B represents a +225% Y/Y surge, aided by favorable investment income as interest rates remain elevated. Airbnb's GAAP profitability has been more variable due to stock-based compensation and one-time charges, including a $70M alternative minimum tax hit in Q1'26.

Revenue Share — Q4 2025

Share of combined reported net revenue across all four companies

Booking Holdings captures ~42% of combined peer revenue in Q4'25, nearly double Airbnb's share, reflecting its superior scale in the hotel and accommodation segment. Trip.com, despite its rapid growth, still accounts for just ~15% of combined revenue — highlighting the scale gap versus the Western incumbents.

Nights Share — Q1 2026

Share of combined nights/room nights booked (Trip.com excluded — not disclosed)

Booking Holdings accounts for ~55% of combined disclosed nights in Q1'26 (338M of 608M), more than Airbnb and Expedia combined — a dominance anchored in European hotel penetration. Airbnb's 26% nights share is notable given its average nightly revenue is significantly higher than hotel OTA peers.

Gross Bookings Share — Q1 2026

Share of combined reported gross bookings (Trip.com excluded — not disclosed)

Booking holds ~46% of combined disclosed GBV ($53.8B of $118.5B), with Expedia at ~30% and Airbnb at ~25%. Airbnb's GBV share is growing — up from an estimated 22% in Q1'25 — as its RNPL-driven ADR expansion boosts bookings value faster than volume.

Destination GBV Mix by Region — 2025

Share of gross bookings by destination region (where guests travel). Airbnb & Booking from reported data; Expedia & Trip.com estimated.

The contrast is stark: EMEA destinations capture 62% of Booking's GBV vs. just 40% for Airbnb and 30% for Expedia, reflecting Booking.com's European hotel heritage. Trip.com is essentially an APAC-only platform at 85% APAC mix, though its international arm is rapidly expanding westward.

International Revenue Share Trend

% of revenue from non-home-market regions annually; Trip.com internationalising fastest

Trip.com has made the most dramatic shift toward international revenue — from ~30% in 2022 to ~47% in 2025 — driven by its global Trip.com brand and Skyscanner expansion. Booking remains the most international at ~87% non-Americas, while Expedia's non-Americas share has held steady at ~35%, reflecting its US-heavy brand portfolio.

Revenue by Region — 2025

USD billions; Booking dominates EMEA, Expedia leads US+Canada, Trip.com leads APAC

The competitive map is highly regional: Booking's EMEA revenue of $16.1B dwarfs all other peers in that region, while Expedia leads US+Canada at $8.9B. Trip.com's APAC revenue of $6.6B gives it structural dominance in the highest-growth market globally.

Gross Bookings by Region — 2025

USD billions; EMEA largest GBV pool driven by Booking's dominance; APAC second-largest

Booking's EMEA GBV of $107B towers over all peers in all regions, underlining why any EMEA-focused travel investment thesis converges on Booking.com. APAC is the second-largest GBV pool at ~$118B combined, led by Trip.com's $54B China-dominated base.

Nights Booked by Region — 2025

Millions; EMEA commands most nights; APAC nights concentrated in Trip.com's China base

Booking's EMEA nights of 750M represent the single largest regional block, nearly 3× Expedia's entire EMEA volume. APAC nights are heavily skewed toward Trip.com's 420M figure, which is primarily domestic Chinese travel — a market the Western OTAs have not meaningfully penetrated.

Regional Revenue Growth — 2024→2025

Y/Y % growth per company per region; APAC and LatAm outpacing mature markets

Booking leads in APAC revenue growth (+14%) among peers with disclosed data, while Trip.com's EMEA outperformance (+18%) signals that its international expansion is gaining real traction. US+Canada remains the slowest-growth region across all peers at 7–11%, consistent with a mature market.

Regional GBV Growth — 2024→2025

Y/Y % GBV growth per company per region; APAC continues to outperform globally

Booking leads APAC GBV growth (+14%) among disclosed peers, suggesting it is capturing share in Asia-Pacific despite Trip.com's home advantage. LatAm shows the second-highest growth across multiple peers (10–11%), indicating emerging markets are becoming a meaningful incremental revenue contributor.

Regional Nights Growth — 2024→2025

Y/Y % nights growth per company per region; APAC nights accelerating across platforms

APAC nights growth of 12–14% at Booking and Trip.com respectively is running well ahead of the EMEA and US+Canada pace of 7–8%, confirming that Asia-Pacific is the structural growth engine of global travel. LatAm nights are expanding at 10%+ for both Airbnb and Booking, outpacing the North American home market.

Regional Growth Trend — Composite Avg

Average Y/Y revenue growth across OTAs by region; APAC consistently fastest-growing

APAC has been the fastest-growing destination region for three consecutive years at 12–15%, even as growth moderated from the 2022–2023 reopening spike. US+Canada is the clear laggard at 7–8% composite growth, reflecting the market's maturity and high penetration levels.

Active Listings / Properties (M)

Annual supply count; Airbnb = active listings, Booking = alt. accommodation listings, Expedia = lodging properties, Trip.com = accommodation listings

Airbnb and Booking are running neck-and-neck in alternative accommodation supply (9.0M vs. 8.7M listings in 2025), a remarkable convergence that underscores Booking.com's aggressive push beyond hotels into STR inventory. Expedia's 3.6M lodging properties reflects a more selective, hotel-first supply strategy.

Supply Growth Y/Y

Annual Y/Y growth in listings/properties; Booking and Airbnb growing fastest

Airbnb's supply growth reaccelerated to +10% in 2024→2025 after slowing to +6% the prior year, driven by host recruitment initiatives in non-US markets. Trip.com's listing growth of +13% in 2025 is notable given its smaller base — pointing to accelerating hotel and home supply additions in China and Southeast Asia.

Nights per Listing — Utilization

Annual nights booked ÷ total listings; proxy for supply efficiency; Trip.com excluded (nights not disclosed)

Booking's utilization of ~138 nights/property is more than 2× Airbnb's ~59 nights/listing, reflecting that hotel properties on Booking.com are professionally managed full-time assets. Airbnb's flat utilization around 59–60 nights suggests stable host activity levels, with new supply additions roughly matching volume growth.

Other Highlights
  • Nights acceleration — +10% Y/Y, up from +9% in Q1'26; broad-based demand across all regions; management noted Q2 momentum continued above prior guidance
  • ADR $184 (+5% Y/Y) — sustained pricing power despite nights volume acceleration; RNPL and larger-home mix continue to support ADR above prior-year levels
  • Reserve Now, Pay Later — ongoing contribution to longer lead-time bookings and higher ADR; live in 20+ markets globally
  • Free cash flow $1.3B — trailing 12M FCF now $4.8B; very strong conversion from revenue to cash with disciplined cost structure
  • FY 2026 guidance raised — at least mid-teens revenue growth (from low-to-mid teens); EBITDA margin ≥35.5%; Q3 revenue guided $4.69–$4.77B (above $4.61B consensus)
  • International mix — non-US nights ~55% of total; EMEA and LatAm continuing to outpace North America; supports structural ADR and supply diversification

  • AI referrals still nascent — AI visibility improving, but AI-driven referrals remain under 1% of room nights; management bullish on long-term conversion opportunity
  • Growth deceleration — room nights +5% vs. +6% in Q1; GBV growth slowing as comps toughen; Q3 guide calls for +3–5% room nights
  • Merchant model gains — merchant share continuing to rise; higher-margin mix supporting EBITDA margin expansion despite slower volume growth
  • Connected Trip — flight, attractions and ground transport attach rates rising; multi-product bookings a growing share of total revenue
  • Cost discipline — management raised cost-savings target to $650M (from prior target); driving operating leverage even as top-line growth moderates

  • B2B momentum sustained — $1.39B revenue (+23% Y/Y), B2B GBV $10.74B (+21% Y/Y); white-label EPS partnerships and Vrbo B2B both accelerating

  • One Key loyalty — cross-brand earn/burn driving higher repeat rates and multi-product attach; management cited improving B2C conversion
  • B2C recovery — B2C gross bookings +8% Y/Y, matching Q1's pace; Core OTA brand (Expedia.com) improving share within the B2C mix
  • FCF acceleration — free cash flow $1.3B in Q2 (+39% Y/Y), significantly exceeding expectations; supports continued buybacks and debt reduction

Beat on all metrics but stock dipped on an antitrust investigation disclosure (SAMR, Jan 2026) and modest near-term guidance vs. elevated growth expectations. International booking growth of +60% remains the core bull thesis; stock trades near 52-week lows at ~9x P/E.
Other Highlights
  • SAMR antitrust investigation — China's State Administration for Market Regulation opened a probe (disclosed Jan 2026); key overhang on valuation, estimated 6–12 month timeline
  • International bookings +60% Y/Y — outbound Chinese travel recovery accelerating; Japan, Europe, and Middle East gaining share of Chinese outbound travel mix
  • Skyscanner integration — driving global flight discovery and cross-sell into accommodation bookings; early funnel data suggests improved conversion vs. standalone Skyscanner
  • International revenue mix expanding — targeting 50%+ international revenue share going forward, up from ~47% in 2025; Trip.com brand scaling fastest in Southeast Asia and Western Europe
  • Valuation dislocation — stock at 52-week lows (~9× P/E) despite +60% international growth and +17% FY revenue; antitrust uncertainty compressing the multiple well below intrinsic value on fundamentals
  • China domestic resilience — domestic hotel and flight bookings remained solid despite macro headwinds, with Q4 2025 domestic volume +15% Y/Y and Chinese New Year 2026 bookings record-high

Performance Deep-Dive

Nights Booked

Total nights booked, millions; Q1 is seasonally weakest, Q3 peaks with summer travel

Airbnb booked 156.2M nights in Q1'26, up +9% Y/Y — the seventh consecutive quarter of positive volume growth since Q1'24. Annual nights have grown from 393.7M in 2022 to 533M in 2025 (+35% cumulative), demonstrating durable demand expansion well beyond the COVID-recovery period.

GBV vs Revenue

Gross booking value vs net revenue, USD billions

GBV expanded to $29.2B in Q1'26 (+19% Y/Y), outpacing revenue growth of +18%, which implies a slight take-rate expansion as ADR-driven bookings carry higher fee revenue. The GBV-to-revenue spread has been broadly stable at roughly 10–11× ratio across quarters.

Average Daily Rate (ADR)

USD per night; reflects pricing and mix across stay types

ADR rose to a record $187 in Q1'26, up +9% Y/Y after dipping -2% in Q1'25 on mix shift toward international and lower-cost properties. The recovery was driven by the Reserve Now Pay Later program (20% of GBV in Q1'26) and a mix shift toward larger homes, which command premium rates.

Revenue · Nights · GBV — Y/Y Growth

Year-over-year % growth across the three core volume and value metrics

The widening spread between GBV growth (+19%) and nights growth (+9%) in Q1'26 is the clearest signal that Airbnb's Q1 reacceleration was ADR-led rather than volume-led. Revenue growth of +18% tracking closely with GBV confirms the take rate has been steady — incremental GBV flows through to revenue at roughly the same rate.

ADR — Y/Y Change

Average daily rate year-over-year %; Q1'25 dipped -2% on mix shift, rebounded +9% in Q1'26

The -2% ADR dip in Q1'25 — the first year-over-year decline since Airbnb went public — was a significant concern at the time, signaling mix pressure from international expansion into lower-cost markets. The sharp +9% rebound in Q1'26 exceeded most expectations and validates that RNPL structurally shifts the booking mix toward higher-value stays.

Long-term Stays Mix (28+ nights)

Long-term stays as % of total nights booked — annual

Long-term stays grew steadily from 18% to 20% of nights booked between 2022 and 2025, representing a durable structural shift toward Airbnb-as-flexible-housing rather than pure vacation rental. Each percentage point shift equates to roughly 5M nights, providing a high-ADR, low-churn demand base that buffers seasonality.

Booking Window Distribution

% of bookings by days-in-advance; last-minute share growing year-on-year; long-range declining — source: AirDNA/industry estimates

The booking window is compressing at both ends — last-minute (≤5 days) grew from 17% to 20% (2023–2025), while the 3-month+ forward-booking segment shrank from 14% to 12%. This dual compression reflects consumer confidence in availability and the rise of flexible travel — though RNPL is now beginning to reverse the short-lead share trend.

Destination Geographic Mix (Destination = where guests travel, not guest origin; 2025 data from Q1 2026 earnings)

Destination GBV Mix — Trend

% of gross bookings by destination region annually; EMEA growing, North America declining

Airbnb's North America destination share declined 6pp in three years (33% → 27%), offset by gains in EMEA (+2pp) and LatAm (+2pp), reflecting deliberate international supply and demand investment. This diversification is positive for GBV growth but introduces downward ADR pressure as lower-cost markets gain share — a tradeoff management is managing via RNPL.

Revenue Mix by Type

Revenue by Type — Stacked

Agency (commissions) · Merchant (transactional) · Advertising (Kayak, OpenTable); USD billions

Merchant revenue — where Booking collects the full booking value then pays suppliers — has grown from ~35% to ~39% of the mix over the period, reflecting management's deliberate push toward a higher-margin, more controllable payment flow. Agency revenue still accounts for ~54% of the total but is declining as a share.

Revenue Mix Share (%)

Booking is actively shifting from agency to merchant model

The agency-to-merchant migration is a multi-year secular trend at Booking — each percentage point shift toward merchant increases Booking's control over the customer payment experience, enabling loyalty programs, BNPL, and ancillary upsell. Advertising remains a stable ~7% of revenue anchored by Kayak's metasearch platform.

Subsidiary Breakdown — Estimated (Booking Holdings does not disclose brand-level financials; figures are analyst & industry estimates)

Room Nights by Brand — Quarterly

Millions; Booking.com dominates ~87%, Agoda ~10% (Asia-Pacific), Priceline ~3% (US)

These are estimated brand-level splits; Booking Holdings does not disclose brand financials. Booking.com's ~87% estimated share underscores its singular dominance within the portfolio — the other brands collectively represent a rounding error in volume terms, though Agoda provides critical APAC optionality.

Gross Bookings by Brand — Annual

USD billions; estimated brand contribution to total GBV

Booking.com's estimated GBV grew from $131B to $162B (2023–2025), a ~24% cumulative gain that tracks closely with the corporate total — confirming the parent's performance is essentially Booking.com's performance. Agoda's growing $18B GBV base reflects genuine Asia-Pacific traction but remains small relative to the flagship brand.

Brand Y/Y Growth — Estimated

Agoda outpacing Booking.com as Asia-Pacific travel recovery continues; Priceline flat

These growth estimates show Agoda accelerating to +13% in 2024→2025 vs. Booking.com's +9%, consistent with the APAC outperformance theme visible in the regional charts. Priceline's near-flat trajectory reflects the saturated US discount travel market — its volume contribution is declining in relative terms.

Brand Geographic Reach

Estimated share of room nights by primary geography — Booking.com (Europe), Agoda (APAC), Priceline (Americas)

Booking Holdings' three-brand geographic architecture is a deliberate diversification — each brand owns its region with minimal overlap, creating a natural hedge against regional downturns. The 58% EMEA concentration via Booking.com is the primary risk; any European travel shock (geopolitical, economic, or currency-driven) would disproportionately impact the holding company.

Nights Booked — All Reported Quarters

Total room nights across all brands, millions; gaps = not reported

Booking's room nights reached 338M in Q1'26, a new quarterly record for a seasonally light quarter and up +6% Y/Y (+8% excluding the Middle East conflict drag). The trend from 298M in Q1'24 to 338M in Q1'26 represents 13% cumulative volume growth in two years — modest but steady in a mature, high-penetration market.

Destination Geographic Mix (Where guests travel; 2025 data from Q1 2026 earnings disclosures)

Destination GBV Mix — Trend

% of gross bookings by destination region; EMEA dominant at 62%, APAC growing fastest (+2pp/yr)

APAC's destination share gained 2pp from 20% to 22% over three years — an incremental but meaningful shift as Asia-Pacific outbound travel (Chinese tourists in Europe, Southeast Asian regional travel) catches up to pre-COVID patterns. EMEA at 62% remains structurally dominant and is unlikely to decline significantly given Booking.com's hotel depth there.

EMEA vs. APAC Destination Share

APAC destination share rising as outbound Asia-Pacific travel recovers; EMEA share gradually ceding ground

EMEA's 40pp share advantage over APAC (62% vs. 22%) is enormous but slowly narrowing as APAC travel volume recovers post-COVID. At the current +2pp/yr APAC pace, parity remains decades away — but the trend confirms Booking is successfully capturing incremental Asia-Pacific demand without sacrificing its European base.

B2C vs. B2B & Brand Breakdown

B2C vs. B2B Revenue

B2C: Expedia.com, Vrbo, Hotels.com, Orbitz · B2B: Expedia Partner Solutions; USD billions

B2B revenue (Expedia Partner Solutions) hit $1.20B in Q1'26, up +25% Y/Y, making it the fastest-growing segment and now representing ~35% of total revenue — up from ~24% in 2022. This structural shift toward B2B reduces Expedia's dependence on direct consumer advertising and provides a more resilient revenue base.

Vrbo vs. Core Brand Nights

Annual nights booked split; Vrbo declined in 2024 vs. core Expedia brands recovering

Vrbo's nights grew modestly from 84M to 86M (2024→2025, +2%), a stark contrast to core brands' +9% growth, reflecting continued share loss to Airbnb in the vacation rental segment. Vrbo's lower take rate (~9% vs. ~13% for Expedia.com) means its slow growth is doubly penalizing to overall margins.

B2C vs. B2B Revenue Growth Y/Y

Quarterly Y/Y %; B2B (Expedia Partner Solutions) accelerating while B2C growth moderates

The divergence is sharpening: B2B reaccelerated to +25% in Q1'26 while B2C slowed to +8% — a 17-point spread. B2B growth is driven by airline and hotel partners adding Expedia's white-label booking tech; B2C deceleration reflects a maturing US consumer market and rising customer acquisition costs via Google/Meta. The gap underlines why EPS is now Expedia's highest-priority growth vector.

Brand-level GBV & Revenue (Expedia does not report brand-level GBV; figures are estimates based on disclosed nights, take-rate assumptions & analyst research)

Gross Bookings by Brand — Annual

USD billions; Expedia.com+Hotels.com consolidating as Hotels.com sunsets; B2B growing fastest. Trivago shown as advertising revenue (CPC-based, not transactional GBV)

These figures are analyst estimates — Expedia does not disclose brand-level GBV. B2B (EPS) GBV grew an estimated 64% from $22B to $36B in just two years (2023→2025), underlining the strategic importance of the B2B channel. Vrbo's flat $14B GBV reflects stagnant volume growth at modestly premium pricing. Trivago (61% owned) contributes ~$0.5–0.6B in metasearch advertising revenue — small in absolute terms but strategically important as a demand-generation funnel feeding back into Expedia's OTA brands.

Revenue by Brand — Annual

USD billions; Vrbo lower take-rate (~9%) vs. Expedia.com (~13%)

The take-rate differential between Vrbo (~9%) and Expedia.com (~13%) means that Vrbo's stagnant volume drags overall margin mix; every dollar of GBV on Vrbo generates ~30% less revenue than on the core OTA brands. The Hotels.com sunset and consolidation into the Expedia.com brand should modestly improve blended take rates over time.

Vrbo vs. Core Nights Y/Y Growth

Vrbo nights declined in 2024 as short-term rental supply moderated; recovering in 2025

Vrbo's -7% nights decline in 2023→2024 was a major investor concern, reflecting Airbnb's superior host network effects and brand recognition in vacation rentals. The modest +2% recovery in 2024→2025 signals stabilization rather than a reversal, while B2B's sustained +20% annual growth is the clear bright spot in the portfolio.

Regional Breakdown (Expedia reports consolidated; regional splits estimated from 10-K geographic disclosures & analyst research)

Revenue by Region — Annual

USD billions; Expedia is Americas-heavy (~65%) vs. Booking's Europe dominance

US+Canada at ~60% of Expedia's revenue is both a strength (high absolute value) and a vulnerability (limited growth potential in a near-saturated market). EMEA at $3.6B is growing at +9% annually and represents the most compelling share-gain opportunity against Booking's entrenched position.

Gross Bookings by Region — Annual

USD billions; EMEA share growing as Expedia expands European hotel supply

APAC GBV grew from $9B to $18B in just three years (2022→2025), a doubling driven by post-COVID Asia-Pacific recovery and Expedia's regional hotel supply expansion. The APAC growth story echoes Booking's own regional trajectory a decade earlier — Expedia is playing catch-up in a market where it remains structurally underweight.

Nights by Region — Annual

Millions; APAC growing fastest from a smaller base

APAC nights grew from an estimated 50M to 53M in 2024→2025 (+6%), modest in absolute terms but the fastest-growing region in Expedia's portfolio. US+Canada at 201M nights dominates and is growing at +6%, but the flat take-rate means Americas GBV growth closely mirrors nights growth — leaving little room for yield expansion without ADR tailwinds.

Regional Revenue Growth Y/Y

EMEA accelerating in 2025 driven by European outbound recovery; LatAm emerging

EMEA reaccelerated to +9% growth in 2024→2025 — the fastest regional growth in Expedia's portfolio — as European travel demand absorbed post-COVID normalization with resilience. LatAm returned to +7% after a flat 2023→2024, suggesting Expedia's historically underinvested LatAm segment may be benefiting from B2B partner expansion in the region.

GBV Growth by Region Y/Y

APAC showed outsized GBV growth 2023→2024 as China outbound re-opened; stabilising in 2025

APAC's GBV growth decelerated sharply from +42% in 2023→2024 to +6% in 2024→2025 — a normalization after the China outbound travel reopening provided an unsustainable base-effect boost. The 2025 deceleration does not imply structural slowdown; the region is reverting to a sustainable mid-single-digit growth trajectory.

Revenue Share by Region (%)

US+Canada share gradually declining as EMEA and APAC grow faster

US+Canada's revenue share has declined from ~60% in 2022 toward ~57% in 2025 as EMEA and APAC grow faster, but the pace of diversification is slow relative to Booking or Airbnb. A more meaningful shift toward non-US revenue would require Expedia to materially increase its EMEA hotel supply and brand recognition — a multi-year undertaking.

Revenue by Product Segment

Revenue by Product — Stacked

Accommodation · Transportation (air/rail) · Packaged tours · Corporate & other; USD billions

Transportation (air/rail ticketing) is Trip.com's largest segment at ~35% of FY2025 revenue ($3.05B), reflecting China's high rail and domestic flight usage relative to standalone accommodation bookings. Packaged tours at ~14% ($1.25B) are growing faster than the corporate average, driven by international group travel demand recovering from zero in 2022.

Domestic vs. International Revenue

China domestic (Ctrip) vs. international (Trip.com brand + Skyscanner); annual, USD billions

International revenue grew from $2.82B to $4.14B (2023→2025, +47%), outpacing China domestic growth of +35% over the same period — making international the faster-growing half of the business for the first time. If current trajectories hold, international will surpass domestic revenue by approximately 2027, a transformational milestone for the company's global positioning.
